tools.name: memory_write
tools.description: Store a memory permanently. Namespaced to YOUR paying wallet — your wallet is your private memory store. Semantic-indexed for later search. Paid: $0.001 per write via x402 (payment in _meta['x402/payment']).

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Semantic search over YOUR stored memories (payer-wallet namespace). Returns top-k by embedding similarity. Paid: $0.002 per search via x402.

tools.name: memory_export
tools.description: Export ALL memories in YOUR payer-wallet namespace (up to 1000, newest first). Your data is yours. Paid: $0.01 via x402.

tools.name: memory_stats
tools.description: FREE: count + last-write timestamp for any wallet namespace. Content is never returned on the free tier.

name: memory_forget
description: Delete memories by id from YOUR namespace (or a namespace you hold a write/rw grant for). Max 100 ids per call. Paid: $0.001 per call via x402.

name: memory_write_free
description: FREE (no payment): store a memory in YOUR namespace, proven by an EIP-191 personal_sign instead of an x402 payment. wallet_auth = base64 JSON {address,ts,signature} where signature = personal_sign of 'borismem-free:<address>:<ts>' (ts within 600s). Writes to the SAME namespace paid calls use. Capped

name: memory_search_free
description: FREE (no payment): semantic search over YOUR namespace, proven by an EIP-191 personal_sign. Same wallet_auth scheme as memory_write_free. Capped at 500 searches / rolling 30 days per wallet.

name: memory_stats
description: FREE: count + last-write timestamp for any wallet namespace. Content is never returned on the free tier.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "memory_write" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Store a memory permanently. Namespaced to YOUR paying wallet — your wallet is your private memory store. Semantic-indexed for later search. Paid: $0.001 per write via x402 (payment in _meta['x402/payment'])." → after: "Store a memory permanently. Namespaced to YOUR paying wallet — your wallet is your private memory store. Semantic-indexed for later search. Optional supersedes=[ids] marks prior memories in your namespace as superseded by this one (excluded from search, still visible in export with their superseded_"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
